title: The training principle series: mind muscle connection
summary: Explains mind-muscle connection: the ability to flex a muscle on command is a limited test, but the useful meaning is being able to prioritise a target muscle within a compound movement so stronger muscles don't take over. He builds it with isolation movements and focusing on the stretch in the negative, and acknowledges the counterargument that more volume and bigger muscles explain the effect.

claims.claim: Mind-muscle connection is the idea that a pathway between brain and muscle lets the muscle receive more activation during an exercise.
He can contract his right pec much more than his left, and his right side is stronger, suggesting some truth to the flex-on-command idea.
Flexing on command is a flawed test because some muscles (rhomboids, mid traps, short head of the biceps) fire in unison with others or react to stretch and cannot be flexed voluntarily.
Whether a muscle must be felt to grow is controversial; critics argue a stretched muscle that stores and releases energy is being worked regardless.
From a hedonistic standpoint, feeling the muscle work is more enjoyable for a bodybuilder than just moving heavy weight.
The real meaning of mind-muscle connection is the ability to prioritise a specific muscle within a compound movement, so the strongest muscles don't cannibalise the work.
On pull-ups, focusing on stretching the target muscle (e.g. lats) during the negative makes it naturally more engaged on the positive; he has found this true repeatedly.
A muscle you can focus on and target during a movement gets more taxed and grows more; this is not proven scientifically but is scientifically sound.
His rear delts, lats and upper traps have poor mind-muscle connection because stronger back areas take over the work.
Just flexing a muscle may help a little, but the easiest way to build mind-muscle connection is isolation movements that light up the area, done before or after compounds to pre-activate it.
His tools: lots of pullovers and wide-grip pull-ups for lats, face pulls and Arnold raises for rear delts, and isometric holds letting the traps stretch for traps.
Once you can immediately tap into a muscle group's fibers, hypertrophy progresses well; he believes the more he focuses on his lats the more they grow.

Counterargument he accepts: extra work to build connection is extra volume and damage, and a growing muscle gains more neural representation so you feel it more; the effect may not be about feeling at all.

exercises.name: Pull-ups
cues: focus on stretching the lats during the negative
exercises.why: makes lats engage more on the positive instead of arms/mid back
